_doc: Single source of truth for Singapore rule values (DEC-013). status: VERIFIED (read on an official page) | CORROBORATED (secondary sources only) | UNVERIFIED | ASSUMPTION (a modelling choice, not a rule). Engine code must never hard-code these. review_due is set to the next scheduled change point (HDB loan rate is reviewed quarterly; CPF changes on 1 Jan).

params.note: gov.sg explainer (last updated 5 Oct 2026): buyers of 'a typical new 99-year lease flat own the rights to their flats for 99 years'. hdb.gov.sg pages tried 2026-10-07 returned 404 or did not state the term in readable text. Short-lease 2-room Flexi (15-45 y, seniors) is a separate option, not this standard term.

Full CPF use only if the remaining lease covers the youngest buyer to 95; otherwise pro-rated. Pro-ration formula is not published (CORROBORATED: usable = min(1, (L-20)/(75-A))) — not used until cross-checked against the CPF housing-usage calculator.
CPF: pro-rated use allowed if remaining lease is 'at least 20 years' (MND/HDB tables say 'more than 20' — exactly 20 is a boundary case).
Lowered from 80% to 75% with effect from 20 Aug 2024. Pro-rated from 75% when the lease does not cover the youngest applicant to 95.
First housing loan; min 5% cash downpayment. Lower tier applies beyond the tenure/age limits.
First housing loan when tenure exceeds 25 y (HDB flats) or the loan runs past age 65 (income-weighted average age).
Bank loans on HDB flats: tenure above 25 y drops LTV to the lower tier.
Absolute tenure cap for bank loans on HDB flats.
HDB loan tenure = shortest of 25 y, 65 minus applicants' average age, remaining lease minus 20 y.
HDB loan repayment period is capped at the remaining lease minus 20 years.
First bank housing loan at the full LTV tier: at least 5% of the price in cash (10% at the lower tier).
First bank housing loan at the lower LTV tier: at least 10% of the price in cash.
HDB: simple average age; MAS (bank): income-weighted average age.
Applies to HDB flats for both HDB and bank loans.
Bank loans only (60% before 16 Dec 2021). Not yet used — needs other-debts input (Phase 1).
HDB assesses the loan at the higher of this floor and the prevailing HDB loan rate.
Residential property: higher of 4% or the 'thereafter' rate (3.5% before 30 Sep 2022).
0.1 pp above the CPF OA rate; may change in Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct. Confirmed 2.60% for Q3–Q4 2026 — re-check each quarter (review_due).
Illustrative bank package rate; not a rule. To become user-editable (Phase 1).

params.unit: [band width S$, rate]; null width = remainder
params.note: On the higher of price or market value; rounded down to the nearest dollar, minimum $1.

params.unit: S$ avg gross monthly household income
params.note: HDB loan + CPF Housing Grant (resale), families; raised from S$14,000 for HFE applications from 24 Aug 2026 (extended families S$24,000).
Single buying alone (S$16,000 with family or other singles); raised from S$7,000 for HFE applications from 24 Aug 2026.
Singles scheme minimum age (21 with a non-resident spouse — not modelled). Effective date approximate.

params.unit: [income band upper bound inclusive S$, grant S$]
params.note: First-timer families; 12-month employment condition; full amount only if the lease covers the youngest core member to 95, otherwise pro-rated (formula not published).

params.unit: [income band upper bound inclusive S$, grant S$]
params.note: First-timer singles; also used for a first-timer + second-timer couple, assessed on half the household income.

params.unit: S$ by flat size (small = 2–4 room, large = 5-room+)
params.note: Amounts read on the official page; effective date from secondary sources. Needs an SC applicant; income within the family ceiling.

params.unit: S$ by flat size (small = 2–4 room, large = 5-room)
params.note: Singles may buy 2- to 5-room resale flats. Effective date from secondary sources.

params.unit: S$ (with = live with parents/child; near = within 4 km)
params.note: No income ceiling; once per household. Effective date approximate (2019 levels unchanged).
Joint buyers: highest applicable rate. Married SC+SC / SC+PR couples buying their first home, and HDB-to-HDB upgraders who must sell within 6 months, may get remission — shown as a note, not applied.
CPF OA may pay stamp duty in full (not counted in the CPF housing limit).
CPF says 'stamp duty' without naming ABSD; treated as included (secondary sources agree).
CPF OA may pay legal fees in full.
Option fee + exercise fee together at most S$5,000; cash only (CPF cannot pay); part of the price. Modelled at the maximum.
Request for Value S$120 + resale admin fee S$80 (3-room and bigger).
Rate-rise scenarios shown in Afford (+1 and +2 percentage points).
Above this share of income (at the test rate) the app calls the loan 'tight'; not a rule.
Conveyancing + registration estimate (CPF cites ~S$2,500–3,000 with a private lawyer; HDB's own conveyancing scale is lower). Editable later.

Modelling choice: a block + flat type needs at least this many approved rentals in the window (12 months, else 24) before its quartiles are used as the comparison; otherwise the town figures are used. Matches the resale benchmark rule (>= 3 sales). Not an HDB rule.

Modelling choice: an asking rent inside the interquartile range of comparable approved rentals is called 'fair'. The data carries only p25 / median / p75, so values are clamped to 25..75 and interpolated linearly between them. Not an HDB rule; HDB does not regulate open-market rents.

params.unit: fraction above the upper band edge
params.note: Modelling choice: asking > upper band edge x (1 + margin) is 'well above'; between the edge and that is 'above'. Not an HDB rule.
Modelling choice: when only a median is known (HDB's quarterly town median, no quartiles), the 'fair' band is median x (1 -/+ halfwidth). Not an HDB rule.

params.unit: minutes [short max, ok max, long max]
params.note: Commute bands: <=30 short, <=45 ok, <=60 long, >60 very long. The 45-minute edge follows LTA's Land Transport Master Plan 2040 target (9 in 10 peak-period Walk-Cycle-Ride journeys under 45 minutes, '45-minute city'); 30 and 60 are modelling choices. Not a rule.

Model parameter (commute estimate, tools/build_commute.py). Adult preferred walking speed is ~1.4 m/s (5 km/h); 4.8 km/h allows for crossings and lights. Used for walk to/from stations, walking transfers and the walk-only alternative.
Model parameter: straight-line distance x 1.3 = walking (or estate-road) path length. Typical urban route-directness ratio 1.2-1.4; the app README already uses 'walking ~ +25%'.

Model parameter: walk to the bus stop + average wait for a feeder/trunk bus when the station (or hub) is too far to walk. Feeder services typically run every 5-10 min in the peak. Bus routes are not modelled individually; access/egress = min(walk, this overhead + road distance / feeder speed).

Model parameter: average in-vehicle speed of a stopping bus on estate/industrial roads, including stops (Singapore bus averages are commonly quoted around 15-20 km/h). Applied to straight-line distance x walk detour factor.
Model parameter: exit/gate to platform plus half the peak headway (trains every ~2-5 min), added once when boarding the first train.

Model parameter: MRT running speed between stations (excluding the per-stop dwell), applied to straight-line inter-station distance x track factor. Calibrated so station-to-station times match journey-planner times: Tampines-Raffles Place ~31 min, Woodlands-Raffles Place ~47 min, Jurong East-one-north ~15 min, Punggol-Paya Lebar ~24 min (rome2rio / singaporemrt.org, retrieved 2026-10-07).
Model parameter: LRT (Bukit Panjang, Sengkang, Punggol) running speed between stations; short hops and tight curves, roughly 2 min per stop with the dwell.
Model parameter: station dwell plus acceleration/braking loss, added per inter-station hop. Calibrated together with commute.rail.mrt_speed_kmh.
Model parameter: rail alignment curvature between consecutive stations (station centroids are joined by straight lines).
Model parameter: interchange walk between platforms plus wait for the next train, per line change (long interchanges such as Dhoby Ghaut or Outram Park take longer, cross-platform ones less).
Model parameter: separately-named stations closer than this are linked as an interchange (e.g. Punggol LRT - Punggol MRT, Bukit Panjang LRT - Bukit Panjang DTL); cost = transfer + walk.
Model parameter (build only): a block may start at any of its N nearest stations by access time (walk or feeder bus); the fastest door-to-door option wins.

params.unit: [[band width SGD of Annual Value, rate], ..., [null, top rate]]
params.note: IRAS Annex A, 'From 1 Jan 2025 onwards': 0% to $12k, 4% >12k-40k, 6% >40k-50k, 10% >50k-75k, 14% >75k-85k, 20% >85k-100k, 26% >100k-140k, 32% >140k. Unchanged for 2026 (IRAS 2026 rebate release changes only the rebate). Same band format as stamp.bsd.bands.

params.unit: [[band width SGD of Annual Value, rate], ..., [null, top rate]]
params.note: IRAS Annex B, Non-Owner-Occupier Residential Tax Rates 'From 1 Jan 2024': 12% first $30k, 20% next $15k, 28% next $15k, 36% above $60k.

params.unit: fraction of owner-occupier property tax; private cap in SGD per year
params.note: One-off 2026 rebate for OWNER-OCCUPIED properties only: 15% for HDB flats, 10% capped at $500 for private. Release title read on iras.gov.sg; the percentages came from search summaries of that release (page body is script-rendered).

IRAS defines AV as the estimated annual rent if let unfurnished; HDB rental approvals include furnished lets. Factor 1 assumed until an IRAS basis is read. Used only when the user has not typed the AV from the IRAS notice (Afford: block rent comps median -> drawn area -> typical rent). Listed in STATE open_decisions.

params.unit: fraction of owner-occupier property tax; private cap in SGD per year
params.note: No rebate announced for 2027 or later as at retrieval; rebates are one-off budget measures, so none is assumed. Replace if a new rebate is announced.

params.unit: SGD per month [low, high] across sampled town councils, by flat type
params.note: S&CC is set by each town council. Read directly: Punggol TC and Tampines TC (both effective 1 Jul 2024; reduced = citizen household without private property, normal = otherwise). Ranges widened with Sembawang, Aljunied-Hougang and East Coast TC rates (East Coast revised Apr 2026) from search summaries. Executive has no reduced rate in most TCs, so reduced = normal range. Multi-generation mapped to EXECUTIVE. Excludes S&CC rebates (U-Save/S&CC rebate months).

params.unit: rule: which households pay the reduced (citizen) S&CC rate
params.note: Punggol Town Council S&CC rates page (w.e.f. 1 Jul 2024), read 2026-10-07: 'Reduced Rates are applicable to citizen households without private property or HDB industrial/commercial property.' Normal rates apply where none of the owners, tenants or authorised occupiers is a Singapore Citizen; where any of them has an interest in private residential, industrial or commercial property; where the flat is owned by or let to a body corporate; or where it is vacant. Same wording in search extracts of other town councils' pages. The app checks the citizen condition (any SC buyer); it has no input for private / commercial property interests, so those cases are explained in the text, not modelled.

params.unit: average monthly household consumption: electricity kWh, water m3
params.note: MSE written PQ reply of 24 Sep 2025, 2024 averages. MSE groups 1-2 room and 5-room/Executive together (values duplicated here). PRIVATE = private apartments and condominiums (landed: 1208.2 kWh, 30.6 m3, not used).

SP Group release (30 Sep 2026) for 1 Oct-31 Dec 2026: household tariff down 3.32 c/kWh (10.4%); 28.59 c/kWh absolute from secondary reports, consistent with SP's 4-room bill drop of $12.99 at ~391 kWh. Revised QUARTERLY; refresh each quarter (next 1 Jan 2027). Gas and U-Save rebates not modelled.

params.unit: SGD per m3 for the first 40 m3 a month, before GST (tariff 1.43 + water conservation tax 0.72 + waterborne fee 1.09)
params.note: PUB press release (Sep 2023): full price from 1 Apr 2025. Average household consumption stays under the 40 m3 tier, so the higher tier is not modelled.
GST 9% from 1 Jan 2024. Applied to electricity and water bills.

params.unit: SGD per year for the stated cover (male, HDB loan)
params.note: CPF example from 1 Jul 2021: male aged 36, $200,000 HDB loan over 30 years pays $209.40 a year. CPF publishes no flat premium table (premium depends on age, gender, cover, term) - the engine scales this example linearly with the loan (ASSUMPTION, indicative only; use the CPF HPS premium calculator for a quote). Premiums are payable for 90% of the cover period (CPF FAQ) and can be paid from CPF OA.

params.unit: SGD per policy term (incl. GST), by flat type
params.note: HDB Fire Insurance (compulsory for flats with an HDB loan) via HDB's appointed insurer Etiqa, premiums from 16 Aug 2024 for a 5-year term. 1-room incl. Community Care Apartment; 2-room incl. Flexi/Studio; 4-room incl. S1; 5-room incl. S2/3Gen; Executive incl. Multi-Generation.
HDB fire insurance premium covers 5 years; renewed every 5 years.

params.unit: annual rate (decimal), 3-month Compounded SORA, daily, by SORA value date
params.note: Computed from the MAS Domestic Interest Rates download (column 'Compound SORA - 3 month', daily) for value dates 1 Oct 2021 - 5 Oct 2026 (5-year window, 1258 days): min 0.1287% (6 Oct 2021), median 2.38315%, max 3.7611% (3 Nov 2023), latest 1.2325% (5 Oct 2026). Historical range, not a forecast. Refresh with the policy review.

params.unit: annual rate (decimal) added to 3M Compounded SORA
params.note: Bank spread over 3M SORA for an HDB-flat floating package. Basis: advertised Sep 2026 packages around SORA + 0.25% in the lock-in years, with spreads typically stepping up afterwards; 0.5% taken as a through-the-loan average. Not a rule; bank-specific.

CPF OA interest 2.5% p.a. for 1 Oct - 31 Dec 2026 (legislated minimum 2.5%; set quarterly). Used as the OA opportunity cost of CPF put into the home and as the accrued-interest rate refunded to OA on sale. Extra interest on the first $60k of combined balances is ignored.

params.unit: years of Minimum Occupation Period before the flat can be sold on the open market
params.note: HDB: resale and Standard flats 5-year MOP (from resale completion for resale buyers); Plus and Prime (PLH) flats 10-year MOP, also for resale buyers of those flats. Read from hdb.gov.sg search extracts (pages are script-rendered). effective_from = Standard/Plus/Prime framework start (Oct 2024 BTO). Private property has no MOP, but Seller's Stamp Duty on early sale is NOT modelled.

params.unit: annual home price growth (decimal) per scenario
params.note: Scenario presets, not forecasts: a mild real decline (-1%), roughly inflation-plus (+2%) and strong (+4%) to bracket outcomes. Ageing leases tend to depress long-horizon resale growth; the user can override.
Rent assumed to track long-run inflation (~2%). Rents are volatile year to year; override with the user's view.

params.unit: annual return on invested cash (decimal), after costs
params.note: Return earned by whichever side has spare cash (the renter's downpayment, the monthly difference). 4% sits between CPF OA (2.5%) and long-run equity returns; a modelling choice, not advice.
Selling costs: agent commission (commonly 1-2% plus GST, negotiable) and conveyancing; rounded to 2% of price. Also deducted from 'today's' equity so year 0 shows what a sale would net.

params.unit: annual home price growth values (decimal) for the sensitivity grid rows
params.note: The three scenario presets plus zero growth.

params.unit: annual investment return values (decimal) for the sensitivity grid columns
params.note: Low (near cash / CPF OA), base, and equity-like returns.

params.unit: spread (standard deviation) of the yearly log change in the home price
params.note: Illustrative spread for the optional Monte-Carlo range in Rent & Buy, not a forecast and not a rule. Each simulated year draws its price growth from a log-normal centred on the chosen price outlook (mean kept), with this spread. Years are drawn independently and not correlated with rents or returns; real prices move in multi-year swings, so real outcomes can spread wider.

params.unit: spread (standard deviation) of the yearly log change in rent
params.note: Illustrative spread for the optional Monte-Carlo range in Rent & Buy, not a forecast and not a rule. Each simulated year draws rent growth around rentbuy.default.rent_growth (mean kept); drawn independently of prices.

params.unit: spread (standard deviation) of the yearly log return on invested cash
params.note: Illustrative spread for the optional Monte-Carlo range in Rent & Buy, not a forecast, not advice and not a rule. Each simulated year draws the return on whichever side has spare cash around rentbuy.default.invest_return (mean kept); a mixed portfolio swings by roughly this much in a year.

params.unit: spread (standard deviation) of the yearly change in the loan rate (decimal), per loan type
params.note: Illustrative, not a forecast and not a rule. Bank loan: year 1 at today's rate, then the rate drifts by a random step each year (never below 0) and the instalment is re-set on the balance left. HDB loan: held at today's rate (0) because the HDB concessionary rate is pegged to the CPF OA rate (rate.hdb.concessionary).

params.unit: decimal per year: spread and cap around the chosen pay rise
params.note: Illustrative spread for the optional Monte-Carlo range on the Plan tab's CPF cards, not a rule. Each simulated future draws one career-average pay rise from a normal around the Plan tab's pay rise, kept within +/- max_dev. CPF interest rates, contribution rates and ceilings are fixed by rule and are not randomised.

params.unit: months of pay: spread and cap around the chosen bonus
params.note: Illustrative spread for the optional Monte-Carlo range on the Plan tab's CPF cards, not a rule. Each simulated future draws one bonus (months of pay per year) from a normal around the Plan tab's bonus, kept within +/- max_dev and never below 0.

Family nucleus: SC applicant with at least 1 other SC or SPR (spouse / fiance(e) / children). HDB page renders with JS; text seen via search extract and the EC eligibility summary on supportgowhere.life.gov.sg. Effective date approximate (long-standing; framework date of the Standard/Plus/Prime classification).

Single Singapore Citizen scheme (age via eligibility.single.min_age): new 2-room Flexi in any location (Standard/Plus/Prime); resale flats of all types except 3Gen, with extra conditions for Plus/Prime. SPR singles cannot buy. HDB official text seen via search extract only. Widowed/orphaned singles from 21 are not modelled.

Non-Citizen Spouse scheme: SC aged 21+ with a non-resident spouse holding an LTVP / work pass valid at least 6 months from issue. 2-room Flexi from HDB; resale flats of all types except 3Gen and Prime (PLH) resale flats. Seen via HDB search extract; the 2-room Flexi income ceiling (S$7,000 pre-NDR 2026) is not modelled.
SC/SPR households pay a S$10,000 premium on a new HDB flat; a S$10,000 Citizen Top-Up is credited to CPF OA when the SPR becomes an SC (apply within 6 months). HDB text via search extract.

SPR households (no SC member) may buy a resale flat only; the buyer and every SPR in the core family nucleus must have held SPR status for at least 3 years at HFE / resale application. No new flats, no new ECs, no HDB loan (needs an SC). HDB text via search extract.
Non-Malaysian SPR households buying a resale flat must be within the SPR quota: 8% block, 5% neighbourhood. HDB text via search extract.

Ethnic Integration Policy limits (Indian/Others raised to 12%/15% in 2010). Government secondary source (SG101 / NLB); the live HDB EIP page was not readable. Shown as context only — the engine cannot know a block's composition.

HDB flats (new or resale) may only be bought by SC/SPR households; foreigners cannot own one except as the non-resident spouse under the Non-Citizen Spouse scheme. Consistent across HDB eligibility pages seen via search; no single page fetched.

value.singles: Joint Singles Scheme, all SC aged 35+

params.note: New EC from the developer: SC applicant plus at least 1 other SC/SPR; singles only under the Joint Singles Scheme (all SC, 35+); no private property owned or disposed of in the 30 months before application. Government summary page (SupportGoWhere) via search extract.
Raised from S$16,000 at NDR 2026 for EC projects whose land tenders close on or after 24 Aug 2026 (older projects keep S$16,000 — not modelled). HDB press release seen via search extract only.

Executive Condominium Housing Scheme Act: an EC may be transferred to an SPR after the 5-year MOP, and to any person 5 years after the MOP ends (10 years from TOP). Statute text via search extract. Whether HDB-style age rules apply to singles buying resale ECs was not checked.

Residential Property Act: any non-citizen (incl. SPR) needs SLA approval to buy landed (restricted) property; SPR applicants should have 5+ years of PR and an exceptional economic contribution. Condominium / non-landed units are not restricted. SLA text via search extract.

HDB housing loan: at least 1 applicant must be an SC, income within the ceiling (eligibility.income_ceiling.*), and fewer than 2 HDB loans taken before. HDB (mynicehome / SupportGoWhere) text via search extract.

From 27 Jul 2026 (with immediate effect) private-property owners / ex-owners buying a non-subsidised resale flat without an HDB loan have no wait-out (was 15 months); any HDB-owned/private property must be disposed of within 6 months of completion. The 30-month wait-out for subsidised purchases, CPF grants, HDB loans and new ECs is from secondary sources plus the EC page — not seen on an HDB page.

HDB tenants: SC, SPR, or non-citizens on an Employment Pass, S Pass, Work Permit (sector rules in rental.wp.sectors), Student Pass, Dependant Pass or LTVP valid for at least 6 months from the owner's application. Effective date approximate.

MOM page (fetched): Malaysian or services-sector WP holders may rent HDB flats; non-Malaysian manufacturing WP holders bedrooms only. Construction / marine shipyard / process (CMP) WP holders must be Malaysian — HDB eligibility text via search extract only, hence CORROBORATED. Effective date approximate.
Bedrooms that may be rented to Work Permit holders: none in 1-2 room, 1 in 3-room, 2 in 4-room or bigger. Effective date approximate.

Non-Citizen quota for whole-flat rental: 8% neighbourhood / 11% block; applies if any tenant is a non-Malaysian SPR or foreigner; Malaysians exempt; not applicable to bedroom rental. Effective date approximate.
HDB rental: minimum 6 months; maximum 3 years per approval (2 years if any tenant is a non-Malaysian non-citizen). Effective date approximate.

Whole-flat rental: SC owners who have met the 5-year MOP; Standard and unclassified (mature/non-mature) flats only — Plus and Prime flats can never be rented out whole; SPR owners never. HDB eligibility page + gov.sg explainer (both fetched).
All owners of 3-room or bigger flats (any citizenship, any classification incl. Plus/Prime) may rent out bedrooms, also during the MOP; not 1-2 room flats. HDB approval required.

Occupancy cap 4 (1-2 room), 6 (3-room), 6 (4-room+), temporarily 8 for 4-room+ from 22 Jan 2024 until 31 Dec 2028 (extended 16 Jan 2026); rental periods running past 31 Dec 2028 revert to 6. Cap counts owners and occupiers as well as tenants (gov.sg / MND text via search extract). MOM + URA pages fetched.
Private homes: 6 unrelated persons (family members and domestic helpers excluded); 8 for properties of at least 90 sqm until 31 Dec 2028, after registration with URA (S$20 fee).
Private residential minimum stay of three consecutive months; no daily/weekly rental. Effective date approximate.

Lease duty: 0.4% of total rent for leases of 4 years or less; 0.4% of 4x the average annual rent (AAR) for longer / indefinite leases; exempt when AAR <= S$1,000; rounded down to the dollar, minimum S$1; pay within 14 days of signing. Based on the higher of contract or market rent. IRAS page renders with JS — text via search extract. Effective date approximate.
HDB e-service to check the Non-Citizen quota of a block / neighbourhood (URL from search results; e-service itself not opened).
OW ceiling S$8,000 from 1 Jan 2026 (S$7,400 in 2025). The 1 Jan 2027 rate table still shows S$8,000 (max S$2,960 = 37% x 8,000).

params.unit: S$ total wages per calendar year
params.note: CPF annual limit; AW ceiling = S$102,000 - total OW subject to CPF in the year. Unchanged since 2016 (effective_from set to the 2026 confirmation).

params.unit: S$ total wages per month (upper bounds, inclusive)
params.note: TW <= $50: nil. $50-$500: employer only (employer_only x TW). $500-$750: employer_only x TW + phase_in x (TW - 500), employee pays phase_in x (TW - 500). > $750: full rates (OW capped at the OW ceiling).

params.unit: share of wages by scheme and age band (see _doc)
params.note: Tables 1-5 (private sector / non-pensionable). full = SC, SPR 3rd year onwards, and SPR 1st/2nd year on an approved full/full joint application. GG = graduated employer & employee; FG = full employer, graduated employee. Age bands use completed years; CPF switches band from the month after the birthday month (up to 1 month difference).

params.unit: share of wages by scheme and age band (see _doc)
params.note: Budget 2026 senior-worker step: 55-60 total 35.5% (employee 19%), 60-65 total 26% (employee 13%); the increase is allocated to the RA up to the FRS. Later years assumed unchanged (no further schedule announced).

params.unit: ratio of total contribution (sa_ra = SA below 55, RA from 55)
params.note: MA computed first, then SA/RA; OA is the remainder. CPF example: $100 at age 30 -> OA 62.17, SA 16.21, MA 21.62; $100 at 57 -> OA 35.30, RA 33.82, MA 30.88. Published for full rates; applied to graduated PR rates too (ASSUMPTION — CPF does not publish separate graduated allocation in this PDF).

params.unit: ratio of total contribution (sa_ra = SA below 55, RA from 55)
params.note: CPF example: $100 at 57 -> OA 33.82, RA 36.61, MA 29.57.
Legislated minimum 2.5% (rate for 1 Oct - 31 Dec 2026). Reviewed quarterly; projections hold it at the floor.
4% floor extended to 31 Dec 2027 (release 22 Sep 2026). Beyond 2027 the floor is an ASSUMPTION (extended yearly since 2008).

params.unit: tiers [cumulative combined balance upper bound S$, extra annual rate]
params.note: Combined balances counted RA, then OA (max $20,000), SA, MA. Extra interest on OA goes to SA (below 55) / RA (55+); on other accounts stays in that account.
Computed monthly, credited and compounded yearly. Contributions earn from the next month; withdrawals stop earning in the month they are made.

RA created on the 55th birthday from SA then OA, up to the FRS; SA closed, SA balance above the FRS goes to OA (SA closure from Jan 2025). Same age switches the extra-interest tiers. Order SA-then-OA is CORROBORATED (page says 'SA and/or OA'). The $5,000 withdrawable OA set-aside is not modelled.
CPF LIFE payout eligibility age (members born 1954 or later); deferral to 70 raises payouts up to 7% a year (not modelled).

params.unit: S$ by year the member turns 55
params.note: FRS = 2 x BRS; fixed for life once the member turns 55. BRS table: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-much-is-my-basic-retirement-sum. 2027 sums announced at Budget 2026 (12 Feb 2026).
ERS raised to 2 x FRS from 1 Jan 2026 (S$440,800 for the 2026 cohort); 1.5 x before.

params.unit: annual growth of BRS/FRS beyond the last published cohort
params.note: Recent published steps: FRS 2024->2025 +3.5%, 2025->2026 +3.5%, 2026->2027 +3.5%. Projection rounds BRS to the nearest S$100; FRS = 2 x BRS.

params.unit: S$ MediSave cap by calendar year (members below 65)
params.note: BHS 2026 S$79,000 (from S$75,500 in 2025). Fixed for life at the BHS of the year the member turns 65. MA contributions above the BHS flow to SA (below 55) / RA (55+), then OA once the SA/RA holds the FRS (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/infohub/educational-resources/2-things-you-should-know-about-your-medisave-savings-once-it-reaches-the-basic-healthcare-sum).
Cohort BHS is fixed in the year the member turns 65.

params.unit: annual growth of BHS beyond the last published year
params.note: CPF adjusts the BHS yearly for healthcare use; 2025->2026 was +4.6%. Projection rounds to the nearest S$100.

Below 55, SA allocations stop at the current FRS and flow to OA; from 55, RA allocations stop at the FRS. The engine uses the current-year FRS below 55 and the member's cohort FRS from 55 (CPF wording 'up to the FRS' — basis not spelled out).

params.unit: S$ RA at 55 -> estimated monthly payout from 65
params.note: CPF's estimates for a male member on the Standard Plan with BRS/FRS/ERS at 55 (no further top-ups). The engine turns these into payout-per-dollar factors on the projected RA at 65 — an estimate, not a CPF quote.

Accrued interest = interest the withdrawn OA savings would have earned, compounding on principal and prior accrued interest; secondary sources state the prevailing OA rate (2.5%), no extra interest. Refunded to OA (below 55) or RA first (55+) on sale.
Annual SRS contribution caps since 1 Jan 2016 (15% / 35% of the S$102,000 income base). Foreigners have no CPF; SRS is their tax-advantaged retirement track.

HDB resale Option Period: 21 calendar days (incl. Sat/Sun & public holidays) after the Option Date; expiry 4pm. Also in HDB Resale Terms & Conditions para 2.3. effective_from = earliest dated example in the notes, not the rule's start.
"The completion date will be within 8 weeks from the date of HDB's acceptance of the resale application, unless extended by HDB." Stored as 8 x 7 days.

Temporary Extension of Stay: at most 3 months from the Resale Completion Date, no further extension; only for sellers who have committed to buy a completed property in Singapore (exercised an OTP or signed an S&P). Needs the buyer's agreement.

params.unit: months from resale completion of the new HDB flat
params.note: HDB resale T&C (buyer section): if the buyer owns any other HDB flat or residential property, it must be disposed of within 6 months from the resale completion date. effective_from is a placeholder (long-standing rule).

IRAS (text via search extract; page body did not render): a married couple (at least one SC) buying a 2nd residential property jointly can get the ABSD refunded if the first is sold within 6 months after the purchase date of the 2nd (completed) or its TOP/CSC (uncompleted), whichever is earlier. No extensions.

params.unit: months after the sale of the first property
params.note: IRAS (search extract): the refund application is made within 6 months after the date of sale of the first residential property.

HDB (mynicehome, updated 23 Aug 2026): for a 2nd HDB housing loan you must first use the full CPF refund and part of the cash proceeds; you may keep S$25,000 or 50% of the cash proceeds (incl. the deposit received), whichever is greater.
See sellbuy.hdb_loan.cash_retain_min: keep the greater of S$25,000 or 50% of the cash proceeds.

params.unit: S$ by type of the subsidised flat sold
params.note: Fixed-amount levy for a first subsidised flat sold on/after 3 Mar 2006, payable when buying a second subsidised flat (BTO / EC from developer). Recipients of the singles CPF Housing Grant pay half (not modelled). Values from HDB text via search extract; page did not render. Resale T&C para 31 confirms the levy applies.

params.unit: [holding period up to N years, rate]; longer = no SSD
params.note: Residential property purchased on/after 4 Jul 2025. MAS: the revised SSD will not affect HDB owners due to the Minimum Occupation Period.

params.unit: [holding period up to N years, rate]; longer = no SSD
params.note: Property purchased 11 Mar 2017 – 3 Jul 2025. Derived from the MAS release: the 2025 change raised each tier by 4 percentage points and extended the period from 3 to 4 years.

HDB news 27 Jul 2026 (title verified; body via search extract): the 15-month wait-out is removed, effective immediately, for private property owners / ex-owners buying a non-subsidised resale flat without an HDB loan. They must still dispose of the private property within 6 months of the HDB purchase.

CPF: for members 55 and above, housing refunds first top up the Retirement Account to the required amount; the excess goes to OA. Order of deductions: housing loan, then CPF refund (principal + accrued interest), then cash; no cash top-up of a refund shortfall when sold at market value.
Seller's agent commission is negotiable and not regulated; 1-2% is commonly quoted. Upper end used so proceeds are not overstated. GST on the commission not added. Editable per call (agentFeeRate).

params.unit: days before granting the Option to Purchase
params.note: "Sellers must have a valid Intent to Sell registered in the HDB Flat Portal at least 7 days before granting an Option to Purchase"; buyers must hold a valid HFE letter when granted the OTP. Resale application: sellers and buyers agree when to submit their portions (no fixed deadline). effective_from = earliest dated example in the notes.

params.unit: working days after the Option Date
params.note: Buyers using CPF and/or a housing loan submit the Request for Value (with page 1 of the OTP) by the next working day after the Option Date.

params.unit: S$ by flat type, at flat booking
params.note: S$500 for a Community Care Apartment or 2-room Flexi, S$1,000 for 3-room, S$2,000 for 4-room, 5-room or 3Gen. Forms part of the downpayment. Same in the Oct 2024 BTO Annex C and mynicehome.gov.sg BTO guide (29 Jun 2026). effective_from = earliest document read, not the rule's start.
The BTO option fee is payable by NETS, debit card or eNETS (AXS) — cash, not CPF.
"HDB will invite flat buyers to sign the Agreement for Lease within nine months after they have booked a flat." Also mynicehome.gov.sg BTO guide (29 Jun 2026).

params.unit: ratio of price, at signing of the Agreement for Lease, by loan type
params.note: HDB loan 10%, bank (FI) loan 20% of the flat price, payable by CPF savings and/or cash; the balance is paid at key collection. Bank loan minimum cash at signing 5% (75% LTV) / 10% (55% LTV) per mynicehome.gov.sg BTO guide (29 Jun 2026) = downpayment.bank.cash_min(.lower_tier). Stamp duty and legal fees are also paid at signing.
"The downpayment is payable by CPF savings and/or cash" (bank loans: cash minimum still applies).

params.unit: ratio of price, at signing of the Agreement for Lease
params.note: From the June 2024 BTO exercise, young couples eligible for deferred income assessment can pay a lower downpayment of 2.5% of the flat price; the balance is payable at key collection. effective_from = 1st of the month of that exercise (day not stated).

Couples where both are first-timers or one first-timer + one second-timer; HFE letter applied for on or before the younger applicant's 30th birthday; uncompleted 5-room or smaller flat. effective_from = page last-updated date (13 Apr 2026).

params.unit: ratio of price at Agreement for Lease and at key collection, by loan type
params.note: The HDB page names the scheme (downpayment in 2 instalments, part at signing, rest at key collection) but the split did not render; older HDB pages (pre-Aug 2024 LTV change) are gone. Read the current table before filling.

params.unit: months after collecting the keys to the new flat
params.note: Flat owners buying from HDB have up to six months after key collection to dispose of the existing flat. A contra facility or temporary loan (if eligible) is available after HDB approves the resale application of the existing flat and is redeemed from its net sale proceeds.
LBS T&C (Dec 2025) top-up table starts at the 'CPF Payout Eligibility Age (now 65)'. All owners must have reached it (HDB LBS page via search extract). effective_from = T&C version date.

Raised from S$14,000 (since 11 Sep 2019) to S$16,000 for LBS, SHB and short-lease 2-room Flexi with the 24 Aug 2026 income-ceiling changes. Article title verified; the seniors' figure comes from secondary reports - HDB/CPF scheme pages still showed S$14,000 in search extracts. Re-check.

params.unit: [youngest owner's age from, minimum lease retained in years]
params.note: HDB LBS page via search extract (page does not render for fetch): 65-69 retain 30 (or 35); 70-74 retain 25+; 75-79 retain 20+; 80+ retain 15+, in 5-year steps up to 35.
Longest retention option for every age band (search extract of the HDB LBS page).
Retention options listed in 5-year steps (15, 20, 25, 30, 35).

params.unit: [owner's age from, RA top-up requirement sole owner S$, each owner when 2+ owners S$]
params.note: LBS T&C para 2.2(a): each owner tops up their own RA to this requirement (applications 1 Jan - 31 Dec 2026; adjusted with the Full Retirement Sum). Insufficient share = whole share goes in. Age at application date. Replace on 1 Jan 2027.

params.unit: S$ per household by flat type
params.note: LBS T&C para 2.5: full bonus when total RA/MA top-ups are at least S$60,000; otherwise pro-rated (S$1 per S$2 / S$4 / S$8 topped up). Once per household.
LBS T&C para 2.5(a)-(b) and 2.2(e) (owners already at the FRS may top up MA / spouse to reach S$60,000).

params.unit: S$ in RA after the top-up
params.note: LBS T&C para 2.4(b): an owner below the CPF LIFE age limit must join CPF LIFE if they have at least S$60,000 in the RA after the top-up.
LBS T&C para 2.4(b),(e): owners below 80 join CPF LIFE; those not eligible (e.g. 80 at application) get Retirement Sum Scheme payouts instead.
LBS T&C para 2.2(c)-(d): after the required top-ups, net proceeds above S$100,000 (combined) top each owner up to the current FRS; the rest is paid in cash.
Official text via search extract (page is client-rendered): at least 1 owner must be a Singapore Citizen aged 55 or above.
Official text via search extract: monthly household income not more than S$16,000; matches secondary reports of the 24 Aug 2026 seniors' ceiling increase (from S$14,000).
HDB release via search extract: a net RA increase of up to S$60,000 qualifies for S$30,000 (S$1 per S$2), CPF housing refunds count. Pro-ration below S$60,000 per secondary sources.

params.unit: S$ net increase in CPF RA
params.note: CPF (updated 25 Mar 2026): commit to a net increase of up to S$60,000 in the RA after right-sizing; no cash top-up needed if CPF housing refunds suffice. Must join CPF LIFE.
Extra cash bonus for right-sizing to a 2-room or smaller flat (incl. Community Care Apartments), regardless of the RA amount committed (HDB release via search extract).
CPF (updated 1 Apr 2026): cash bonus of up to S$40,000 when moving to a 3-room or smaller flat.

params.unit: S$ Annual Value of the private property sold
params.note: SHB covers selling an HDB flat (MOP met) or a private property with Annual Value not exceeding S$31,000.

Official text via search extract: book the new flat / apply to buy the resale flat before the sale, or within 12 months of completing it; apply for SHB within 1 year of completing the second transaction.
MOH/HDB 12-13 Jul 2026: lowered from 65 to 55 with effect from the October 2026 BTO sales exercise (effective_from set to 1 Oct 2026; exact launch date not stated).
Short-lease 2-room Flexi: all buyers and spouses at least 55 at application. effective_from = page date.
Lease in five-year increments from 15 to 45 years (also HDB guide for seniors, updated 13 Apr 2026).
The lease must cover the youngest owner (and spouse) until at least age 95.
Seniors' ceiling for short-lease 2-room Flexi raised to S$16,000 on 24 Aug 2026 (secondary reports of the HDB announcement; article body did not render). Singles' ceiling may differ - not modelled.

params.unit: children born 2 Jan Y to 1 Jan Y+1 register in Y+6 and start P1 in Y+7
params.note: MOE (updated 11 Sep 2026): the 2026 exercise (P1 in 2027) is for children born between 2 January 2020 and 1 January 2021, both inclusive; the year-offset rule is generalised from that example. MOE is changing the framework from the 2027 exercise (P1 in 2028).

params.unit: calendar months of the registration exercise (June to August)
params.note: MOE: the 2026 exercise runs from June to August in phases 1, 2A, 2B, 2C and 2C Supplementary; exact phase dates are announced each year. Later years assumed similar.

params.unit: km home-school distance bands (within 1 km, 1-2 km, outside 2 km)
params.note: MOE (updated 11 Sep 2026): priority for SCs (then PRs) living within 1 km, between 1 km and 2 km, and outside 2 km of the school. How MOE measures the distance is not stated on the page; the app shows straight-line distance from the block.

params.unit: rule: HDB-loan LTV when the remaining lease does not cover the youngest buyer to cpf.lease.cover_to_age
params.note: MND-MOM joint release 9 May 2019: the HDB-loan LTV limit 'is pro-rated based on the extent that the remaining lease can cover the youngest buyer to the age of 95'. No formula published; Annex B example 3 (two buyers aged 25, 65-year lease, covers to 90) shows LTV 90% -> 81% (the CPF ratio 90% applied to the then-90% LTV). A CORROBORATED formula ratio = (L - 20) / (75 - A) fits the CPF and MOM examples but is not on an official page. Not computed: the app shows the full-LTV loan as 'up to' with a note.

params.unit: rule: CPF usage limit when the remaining lease does not cover the youngest buyer to cpf.lease.cover_to_age
params.note: CPF (page updated 6 Jul 2026): pro-rated by the youngest owner's age and the remaining lease (at least 20 years); example: two buyers aged 25, 65-year lease, S$550,000 -> up to S$495,000 (90%). The page points to the CPF housing usage calculator; no formula is published. Not computed: CPF use is shown as 'up to' with a note.

params.unit: rule: Enhanced CPF Housing Grant when the remaining lease does not cover the youngest core member to cpf.lease.cover_to_age
params.note: HDB: the full EHG needs the remaining lease to cover the youngest buyer to 95, otherwise it is pro-rated; formula not published (see grant.ehg.family note). DEC-016 Q2: shown as 'up to S$X - HDB will pro-rate, actual amount lower' and the verdict is at least 'tight'.

params.unit: km (PHG 'live near': parents / child within this distance of the resale flat)
params.note: HDB's MyNiceHome guide (page updated 23 Aug 2026): 'Your parents/ child must live in an HDB flat or private residential property that is within 4 km of the resale flat you are buying.' The HDB PHG page (grant.phg source) renders its text by script and could not be read here. HDB checks the exact distance with its own tool; the app uses straight-line distance and says so near the limit. Effective date = grant.phg's.

params.unit: weeks HDB usually takes to process an HFE letter application (complete documents)
params.note: Phase 7b B9 / O11: search extracts say 'about a month' after HDB has the full set of documents (longer around sales launches), but the HDB page did not render for reading on 2026-10-07. Key dates shows no typical weeks until this is read on the official page.

params.unit: working days for HDB to accept a complete resale application
params.note: Phase 7b B9 / O11: search extracts say HDB accepts a complete resale application within 28 working days and documents are ready about 3 weeks later; the HDB pages returned 404 / script-only content on 2026-10-07. Not shown until read on an official page. Completion (8 weeks from acceptance) is already sourced: sellbuy.resale.completion_days.
